name: Mod Super Video
description: Advanced video player with controls, integrations, and detailed reports.
description_html:
With the aim of providing a more dynamic and customizable teaching experience, I present the Super Video Module, a tool that enhances Moodle's capabilities by allowing easy addition of YouTube, Google Drive, or Vimeo videos.

A notable feature of Super Video is its adaptability to Moodle. The video player automatically adjusts its width to avoid inconveniences, ensuring that the content is displayed in an optimized manner-neither too small nor excessively large. Say goodbye to the small and ugly YouTube player...

Additionally, Super Video prioritizes the continuity of student progress. The system automatically saves the point where the student left off, providing a seamless and personalized learning experience. When the student returns to the video, the player automatically positions them at the exact point where they paused, eliminating the need to search manually.

An additional innovation is the visual map bar located below the video. This bar provides a visual representation of the actual percentage of the video that the student has watched. This approach prevents the student from skipping to the end of the video without consuming all the content, promoting more careful viewing and a deeper understanding of the material.

Support for Distraction-Free Design

We are excited to announce that Moodle Mod Supervideo now offers support for Distraction-Free Design, addressing a recent community request (see issue #34).

The Distraction-Free Design has been developed to provide a more focused and immersive viewing experience, allowing users to watch videos without additional distractions. With this new feature, the interface elements have been simplified and reorganized, creating a cleaner and more minimalist environment.

Integration with OttFlix

The Super Video plugin now offers full integration with OttFlix, a secure video hosting and streaming platform equipped with advanced protection technologies against copying and piracy.

If you don't yet have an OttFlix account and want to protect your video lessons with DRM, dynamic watermarking, and full compatibility with Moodle™ Software, get in touch to request access to the platform.

Once your account is created, you can start uploading your videos directly to OttFlix and use them securely in your courses, ensuring a safe and reliable experience for your students.

Kapture

Now, it's possible to record both microphone and system audio, offering a complete experience. With features such as countdown, camera reversal, and camera size configuration, Kapture makes the creation of video lessons and tutorials more flexible and adaptable to the teacher's needs.

Furthermore, uploading slides, documents, and spreadsheets while recording the video lesson facilitates the incorporation of additional material, enriching the teacher's experience.

Kapture offers an integrated and efficient approach to video lesson production, simplifying the process and enhancing the options available to teachers in the Moodle environment.

Reports

Additionally, the Super Video generates comprehensive reports, providing instructors with valuable insights into student views and view maps. This detailed analysis enables continuous adjustments to the content and pedagogical approach, ensuring effective delivery of the material.

Global Settings

For administrators, the global settings functionality offers comprehensive customization. It is possible to set default fields for all videos, ensuring consistency throughout the learning environment. However, flexibility is not compromised, as instructors have the freedom to modify these data for specific videos without affecting global settings.

To access these settings, simply navigate to the Site Administration section, select "Plugins," then "Activity Modules," and finally choose "Super Video." Here, customization options are at your fingertips, allowing refined adaptation to the specific needs of each course.

name: Alternative File System
description: Store files on external services and optimize the platform infrastructure.
description_html:
Alternative File System

Move moodledata/filedir to the cloud and have Moodle serve/read files directly from remote storage-reducing pressure on local disks and making scalability easier.

" Supported today
AWS S3 and DigitalOcean Spaces (S3-compatible).
🚀 Focus

Tip: if you already use tool_objectfs, there’s a migration path designed for a smooth transition.
Practical results
Infra-friendly
'
Less local disk
Takes pressure off the server’s storage and simplifies operations.
📈
Scale without painful migrations
Grow capacity in the bucket/Space-no "surprise disk swap".
🛡️
More resilience
High availability and durability typical of object storage.
⚡
Performance (with CDN, when applicable)
Files in S3/Spaces can benefit from CDN and edge delivery.
Ideal for sites with a large volume of files and a need to reduce Moodle’s "disk cost".
' Security and governance
Control access and policies directly in the bucket/Space: encryption, auditing, least-privilege permissions, and environment isolation.
🧩 Operational simplicity
Less local disk maintenance, less impact from infrastructure upgrades, and more predictable scaling.
🌍 Ready for distribution
A great fit for cluster scenarios and multi-node environments-object storage becomes the shared "common point" for files.

What this plugin does

Moodle stores files in moodledata/filedir. In large environments, this becomes a cost and complexity hotspot: constantly growing local disks, heavier backups, forced storage expansion, and operational risk.

With the Alternative File System, you move those files to remote storage (e.g., AWS S3 or DigitalOcean Spaces), and Moodle starts to read/serve the files remotely.

Result: a more scalable and resilient file base, with simpler and more predictable infrastructure operations.

Compatibility / Storage
  • AWS S3 Supported
  • DigitalOcean Spaces Supported
  • S3-compatible Depends on the endpoint
  • CDN Optional
If you want, you can also adapt it for other S3-compatible providers (just endpoint + credentials).

Features you get

📦 Filedir migration
Moves your existing files from moodledata/filedir to the cloud, with a controlled and verifiable process.
🔁 Migration from tool_objectfs
The plugin can read the tool_objectfs configuration and ease the transition (without reinventing everything from scratch).
🧠 Fewer local storage bottlenecks
Reduces local disk growth and the impact of server maintenance/physical expansion.
🌐 Better global delivery (when using a CDN)
Remote storage + CDN can reduce latency and improve the experience for students in different regions.
🔐 Security best practices
Least-privilege permissions, rotatable keys, bucket/Space policies, and encryption options in transit/at rest.
🧰 Predictable operations
Storage becomes a service: easier to plan cost, capacity, redundancy, and availability.

name: Kopere BI
description: More than 100 dashboards and reports for intelligent data management.
description_html:
Kopere BI is a reporting and dashboard plugin for Moodle with more than 100 ready-to-use reports.

It helps administrators, managers, instructors and educators understand Moodle data through visual dashboards, charts, tables, maps and information blocks. The plugin was designed to make Moodle reports easier to access, easier to read and more useful for decision-making.

Kopere BI can be used to analyse students, courses, enrolments, revenue, access logs, grades, activities, quizzes, forums, SCORM packages, assignments, feedback, competencies, badges and other important learning indicators.

More than 100 Moodle reports

Kopere BI includes a large collection of reports organised by category. These reports are designed to help institutions monitor learning activity, student progress, course usage and administrative indicators directly inside Moodle.

  • Students 9 reports
  • Courses and content 16 reports
  • Login reports 2 reports
  • Dashboard 1 report
  • Online users 1 report
  • Enrollments and revenue 6 reports
  • Users and learners 16 reports
  • Instructors and tutors 10 reports
  • Grades and assessments 3 reports
  • Activities 7 reports
  • Questionnaires and quizzes 11 reports
  • Forums 6 reports
  • SCORM 3 reports
  • Assignments and submissions 2 reports
  • Feedback and surveys 2 reports
  • Competencies, learning plans and badges 5 reports
  • Communication and resources 5 reports

Main purpose

Kopere BI was created for Moodle sites that need practical reports without depending only on raw database queries or standard Moodle reports.

It is especially useful for schools, universities, companies and training providers that need to monitor learning indicators in a more visual and organised way.

Features

Kopere BI provides different ways to display Moodle data, from simple summary cards to advanced interactive reports.

Visual dashboards

Reports can be organised into dashboards, making it easier to follow key indicators in one place. Dashboards can include charts, tables, maps, information cards and custom HTML layouts.

Charts and visual reports

Kopere BI uses ApexCharts to display interactive and responsive charts. These charts help users quickly understand trends, comparisons and distributions.

  • Area charts: useful for showing trends over time, such as student progress, course activity or access volume.
  • Column charts: useful for comparing courses, groups, categories, modules or other indicators.
  • Line charts: useful for following changes over time and identifying patterns in activity, completion or performance.
  • Pie charts: useful for showing proportions, percentages and distributions.

Interactive tables

Kopere BI can display report data in interactive tables using DataTables. This is useful for reports with many records, such as users, courses, enrolments, completions, logs, grades or financial data.

  • Pagination: splits large reports into pages.
  • Search and filtering: helps users quickly find specific information.
  • Column sorting: makes it easier to compare and organise data.
  • Export options: allows data to be exported for external use.

Export options may include print, PDF, Excel, CSV and copy to clipboard, depending on the report configuration.

Information cards

Reports can also be displayed as small information blocks. These blocks are useful for showing key numbers such as total users, active students, completed courses, pending activities, revenue indicators or other important metrics.

Custom HTML reports

Kopere BI supports custom HTML output with Mustache. This allows each report to have its own layout and visual presentation.

With Mustache templates, the same data can be presented as cards, lists, summaries, dashboards or any other layout required by the institution.

Maps

Kopere BI can display map-based reports, including user location information based on IP data when available.

Examples of use

  • Monitor student engagement and access.
  • Analyse course activity and content usage.
  • Follow enrolments, learners and revenue indicators.
  • Track grades, assessments and completion progress.
  • Review quiz, questionnaire, forum, SCORM and assignment activity.
  • Create management dashboards for Moodle administrators and coordinators.
  • Present Moodle data in charts, tables, cards, maps and custom layouts.

Who is this plugin for?

Kopere BI is intended for Moodle administrators, course managers, educators, coordinators and institutions that need clearer and more flexible reports.

It is useful for anyone who needs to understand Moodle data without relying only on technical database access or isolated standard reports.

name: Slow Queries
description: Identify slow queries and find opportunities to improve performance.
description_html:
local_slow_queries is an admin-only plugin that turns your mdl_log_queries table into a practical UI to find, triage and analyze slow SQL statements executed by Moodle.

It focuses on three daily workflows:

  • List & filter slow queries quickly (default exectime > 3s).
  • Open details with SQL + parameters and a ready-to-use ChatGPT prompt including table schemas.
  • Use dashboards to see patterns: top slowest, recurrence, distribution, CRON vs WEB, by qtype, and errors.

Access is restricted to: require_capability("moodle/site:config", context_system::instance())

Data source

The plugin reads from:

Table: mdl_log_queries

Fields used by the UI:

  • id - unique identifier
  • qtype - query type (stored by your logger)
  • sqltext - SQL statement text
  • sqlparams - parameters (string representation)
  • error - non-zero marks error
  • info - optional extra data
  • backtrace - string backtrace
  • exectime - decimal seconds
  • timelogged - unix timestamp
  • timelogged, exectime, qtype, error

Backtrace "caller" logic

The list view shows a simplified "caller" derived from backtrace:

  1. Find the first frame containing /lib/dml/
  2. Show the next frame (usually the Moodle component that invoked the DB layer)
  3. Shorten long absolute paths to keep it readable in a table

This is intentionally pragmatic: it helps you quickly identify whether the query comes from completion, search indexing, forum reports, etc.

CRON detection

A query is considered "CRON" when its backtrace contains:

  • /admin/cli/cron.php

The UI then:

  • sets the CRON column "
  • adds a CRON badge

Parameter handling

sqlparams in production can vary depending on the logger implementation. This plugin attempts to parse common formats:

  • JSON arrays/objects
  • PHP serialize() format
  • "var_export-like" output (example: array ( 0 => 4, 1 => 50, ))

Then it applies parameters to SQL by replacing positional ? placeholders sequentially.

Notes:

  • This is a best-effort representation for analysis and reproduction.
  • It is not intended to be a perfect SQL reconstitution for every edge case.

UX & UI choices

This plugin intentionally keeps a light and readable look:

  • Cards with rounded corners
  • Soft shadows
  • Badges for quick categorization (CRON / WEB / ERROR)
  • Progress bars for distribution/share reports

It relies on Moodle’s loaded Bootstrap styles and adds minimal SCSS.

Security model

  • Pages are accessible only to users with:
    • moodle/site:config in context_system

This is critical because the plugin can reveal:

  • raw SQL
  • parameters (potentially containing sensitive values)
  • file paths in backtraces

Typical usage patterns

Ops triage

  • Open index.php
  • Filter exectime >= 10
  • Identify CRON-heavy spikes or web-timeouts
  • Open details, extract candidate indexes

Regression monitoring

  • Check last 7 days volume
  • Compare max/avg trends weekly
  • Identify new callers (components) from backtrace changes

description_html:
Goal
Stop sending "ugly default Moodle emails" and gain a clean, branded, customizable email system.

Kopere Email

message_kopereemail is a Moodle message output based on message_email, built to deliver consistent, branded emails - while still letting you create fully custom HTML per notification type.

What the plugin solves (in practice)

Moodle can send many different notifications, from many plugin. This plugin adds the missing layer: control, consistency, and customization without core changes or theme hacks.

Standardize identity

How it works

The plugin adds a customization layer on top of Moodle’s existing messaging flow. It decides what to send based on provider and available HTML, then standardizes the final output with the wrapper.

Rule of thumb
  • If fullmessagehtml exists ' apply wrapper.
  • If it doesn’t ' create simple HTML from text, then apply wrapper (if configured).
To prevent students from receiving duplicate emails, the plugin can migrate settings to "take the place" of default email output.
  • Copies existing config from message/email into message_kopereemail.
  • Rewrites provider enabled flags from email ' kopereemail.
  • Locks providers (*_locked = 1) to keep consistency.
  • Disables old email processor in mdl_message_processors.
Import / Export settings
Move wrapper + per-provider templates between environments (staging ' production) or across sites.
  • Exports global wrapper.
  • Exports custom messages per provider (component + name).
  • Does not overwrite Moodle operational preferences like enabled/locked flags.

Available placeholders

Templates use Mustache-style placeholders. Use triple braces when inserting HTML.

Common
  • {{subject}}
  • {{fullmessage}}
  • {{{fullmessagehtml}}}
  • {{dates.now}}
Site

  • {{site.shortname}}

Users to

Users from

  • {{userfrom.fullname}}
  • {{userfrom.firstname}} / {{userfrom.lastname}}
  • {{userfrom.email}}
Course (when detectable)
  • {{course.id}}
  • {{course.fullname}}
  • {{course.shortname}}
  • {{course.url}}
Suggested expansion (roadmap ideas)
If you want to expand the placeholder library, these are high-value additions that keep templates simple:
  • Course completion details: completion date, grade, certificate URL, time spent.
  • Course metadata: category name, start/end date, visibility, custom fields.
  • Recipient convenience: preferred language, timezone, profile fields (safe subset).
  • Sender context: role name in course, department/campus (if available).
  • Utility formatting: preformatted dates, safe links, "short excerpt" from long messages.
  • CTA links: "Go to course", "Open activity", "Message preferences" URLs as ready-to-use placeholders.
Template tip
Insert HTML with {{{variable}}} (triple braces). Using only {{variable}} may escape HTML and print tags as text.

Screenshots

Real UI views: wrapper editor, provider custom templates, and results.
Back to top

Final email result
The student receives a clean, branded email instead of Moodle’s default layout.
Testing workflow
Create/edit a template ' save ' use template preview/test email ' adjust until perfect.

Support

Open GitHub Issue Contact
Best practices
  • Start with the wrapper: set the global identity first.
  • Customize only the providers that matter.
  • Keep templates objective and scannable.
  • Validate HTML structure (close tags properly).
  • Always test after saving.
Why this approach works
  • No core modifications.

  • Centralized admin management.

  • Optional per-provider perfection.

name: Child Course
description: Organize related courses and present access to child courses as an activity.
description_html:
Child course

mod_childcourse adds a Moodle activity that works as a shortcut inside a parent course. When clicked, the user is redirected to a child course and (optionally) the plugin performs automatic enrolment, group mapping, and incremental synchronization of completion and grades.

Auto enrol Groups Completion rules Incremental sync Mobile support
Mental model
Parent course contains a "Child course" activity ' user clicks ' (optional enrol + group mapping) ' redirect to the child course.
Tip: replace this image with your plugin banner or a screenshot of the activity configuration / teacher dashboard.

What the plugin solves (in practice)

Moodle can link courses in many ways, but most solutions become fragile when you need controlled access, consistent group mapping, and reliable tracking. This module adds the missing layer: enrolment rules + stateful synchronization inside a single activity.

Clean shortcut inside the parent course
A single activity points to the child course, with optional "open in new tab" to streamline navigation.
Automatic enrolment (optional)
Enrol users when they access the activity, preserving roles and reducing "permission error" friction.
Group mapping that makes sense
Enrol into a specific group or inherit groups from the parent course to the child course (optional).
Incremental sync (completion + grades)
A scheduled task keeps state and syncs changes incrementally, avoiding "full rebuild" runs.
Designed for real courses
  • Supports Backup/Restore.
  • Can hide the child course from "My courses / Overview" to reduce clutter.
  • On delete, choose whether to unenrol link-enrolled users or keep enrolments.

How it works

The module stores configuration in the instance table and tracks the operational mapping/state in dedicated tables. On access, it optionally enrols and maps groups, then redirects the user. Synchronization runs on schedule (and can be forced manually).

Student access flow
  1. User opens "Child course" activity.
  2. If enabled: enrolment is performed (role preserved if configured).
  3. Optional: group mapping (fixed group or inherited groups).
  4. Redirect to the child course (same tab or new tab).
Important
If automatic enrolment is disabled, the user must already have permission to access the child course, otherwise Moodle will show a permission error in the child course.
Teacher / manager tools
  • Manual sync action (when the user has permission) for immediate incremental sync.
  • Manage instances via a course management page (requires moodle/course:update).
  • Index page listing all instances inside the course.
Plugin pages
  • view.php - main activity page (student redirects; teacher sees a dashboard)
  • manage.php - lists/manages instances in the course
  • index.php - lists module instances in the course

Activity completion rules

When Moodle completion is set to Automatic, the activity can mark itself complete using additional rules based on the child course.

None
The plugin does not automatically control completion for this activity.
Course completed
Marks the activity complete when the user completes the child course.
All activities
Marks the activity complete when the user completes all trackable activities in the child course (per plugin logic).
Note
The child course must have enablecompletion = 1 for completion-based rules to work.

Synchronization (grades and completion)

Synchronization is designed to be incremental. Instead of recalculating everything, the plugin tracks state and updates only what changed.

Scheduled task
The task \mod_childcourse\task\sync_task runs by default every 15 minutes (see db/tasks.php) and performs incremental synchronization for all instances.
Operational idea
Keep a state cache per user/instance and sync only deltas to reduce load on large sites.
Manual sync
On the activity page (for users with permission), a Sync button/action forces an immediate incremental run.
  • Useful after configuration changes.
  • Useful for debugging or support.
  • Does not require waiting for cron schedule.

Mobile support (Moodle App)

In the Moodle App, the activity renders a simple screen with a single button to open the child course. Clicking it performs the same enrolment + access flow as the web version.

Mobile UI rule
Keep it minimal: one button, no noise - fast, reliable, and easy for students.

Data structure (tables)

The plugin uses dedicated tables to keep configuration clean and synchronization scalable.

{childcourse}
Instance settings (including completion rules and sync timestamps).
{childcourse_map}
Tracks enrolments / groups created per instance and per user.
{childcourse_state}
State cache for incremental synchronization (grades / completion).
Why this matters
Separating "settings", "mapping", and "state" prevents slow scans and keeps sync predictable as enrolments grow.

Support

For questions, bugs, improvements, or suggestions, open an issue with enough context to reproduce.
Back to top
When opening a ticket, include
  • Moodle version
  • Steps to reproduce
  • Which activity instance (parent course + child course IDs)
  • Whether auto-enrol / groups / role-preserve were enabled
  • Cron / task logs (if it’s about sync)
Open GitHub Issue Contact
Best practices
  • Enable auto-enrol when you want a "one-click access" experience.
  • Use group mapping to keep cohorts consistent across parent/child courses.
  • Prefer incremental sync for large sites (avoid manual full sync habits).
  • Test completion rules on a staging site before rolling to production.
Why this approach works
  • No core modifications.
  • Single activity UX inside the parent course.

name: Scientific Calculator
description: Scientific calculator available as an activity within courses.
description_html:
Scientific Calculator

This is a Moodle activity module that adds a clean, fast, scientific calculator directly inside your course - perfect for math, physics, engineering, finance, and STEM training where students need a reliable tool without leaving the LMS.

What the plugin solves (in practice)

In many courses, students constantly switch tabs to external calculators. This activity keeps them focused, consistent, and productive - with a calculator always available inside Moodle, without relying on third-party sites or extensions.

Calculator inside the course
Students can compute expressions during lessons, quizzes, and homework - without leaving Moodle.
Scientific functions included
Trig, logs, powers, roots, factorial, constants and more - accessible with one click.
Safe evaluation (no eval)
Expressions are parsed and evaluated using a controlled algorithm - safer than typical eval-based calculators.
Simple history & reuse
A local calculation history lets students click results to reuse them instantly.
Best part
It works as a regular activity: add it once to the course and students can use it immediately - no extra accounts, no external sites.

How it works

The activity renders a Mustache template and loads a lightweight AMD module that handles input, parsing, and calculation entirely in the browser (client-side). That means fast interaction and no server load for each key press.

Rule of thumb
  • Type an expression ' press Enter or =.
  • Functions insert as sin(, sqrt(, pow( to speed up usage.
  • History items are clickable ' reuse results instantly.
Safe expression evaluation
Instead of using eval(), the calculator processes the expression with:
  • Tokenization (numbers, identifiers, operators)
  • Shunting-yard algorithm (infix ' RPN)
  • RPN evaluation with a strict operator/function set
Designed for teaching workflows
Ideal for STEM courses that need quick calculations during learning and practice.
  • Add to any topic/week or section.
  • Works great alongside PDFs, lessons, and problem sets.
  • No personal data storage (privacy-friendly default).

Supported functions & constants

Expressions support common scientific operators, constants, and functions. Use ^ for power and ! for factorial. Constants are case-insensitive.

Operators
  • + - * / % ^
  • Parentheses: ( )
  • Factorial: !
Constants
  • pi (π)
  • e (Euler’s number)
Trigonometry
  • sin(x) cos(x) tan(x)
  • asin(x) acos(x) atan(x)
Algebra & logs
  • sqrt(x) abs(x) exp(x)
  • ln(x) log(x)
  • pow(a,b) min(a,b) max(a,b)
  • floor(x) ceil(x) round(x)
Tip
Use parentheses to keep expressions readable (e.g., sin(pi/2)+sqrt(9)*2).

Support

For issues and improvements, open a GitHub issue including: Moodle version, steps to reproduce, expression examples, and browser console logs (if relevant).

Open GitHub Contact
Best practices
  • Keep the calculator name clear (e.g., "Calculator (Math Support)").
  • Place it near problem sets and formula resources.
  • Encourage students to write expressions with parentheses.
  • Use examples in the activity description for faster onboarding.
Why this approach works
  • No core modifications.
  • No external dependencies.
  • Fast and responsive client-side UX.
  • Privacy-friendly by default (no student data stored).
  • Easy to extend (RAD/DEG, memory keys, saved history, exercises).

name: Public Sitemap
description: Generate an organized public sitemap to improve navigation and discovery.
description_html:
local_kopere_sitemap is a Moodle plugin that automatically generates a public XML sitemap for the site and adds a reference to the sitemap in the <head> of all Moodle pages.

The plugin’s purpose is to make it easier for search engines to index your Moodle site (Google, Yahoo, DuckDuckGo, etc.), allowing crawlers to find relevant public pages on the platform, such as open courses, categories, forums, and homepage content.

The sitemap is generated dynamically from the existing data in the Moodle database and respects content visibility settings.

How the plugin works

The plugin has two main components:

  1. XML Sitemap Generator
  2. Automatic injection of the sitemap link into the site’s <head>

These two mechanisms work together to allow search engines to discover and index the platform’s public content.

Public XML sitemap

The sitemap is available at the following URL:

https://yourmoodle.com/local/kopere_sitemap/sitemap.php

This page generates a valid XML file following the Sitemap protocol standard:

The administrator can choose which types of content should be included in the sitemap.

Site front page

https://yourmoodle.com/

Example:

https://yourmoodle.com/course/index.php?categoryid=3

Courses open for enrollment

  • category is visible
  • has an active enrollment method
  • usually with self-enrollment

Example URL:

https://yourmoodle.com/course/view.php?id=10

https://yourmoodle.com/blog/index.php?entryid=54

description: Manage recurring certification cycles while preserving auditable learner history before progress and selected data are reset.
description_html:
Recertification with auditable history

Recertification manages recurring certification cycles in Moodle while preserving the learner's previous history before progress is reset. Each recertification cycle links archived activities, copied files, execution logs and notifications so the institution can review what existed before a new cycle began.

The execution model first creates the configured history snapshots and validates file archives. Only after the preservation steps succeed does the plugin clean the selected learner data. The operation runs with Moodle locks and a delegated transaction so a failure does not leave a partially reset cycle.

Configurable tasks and scheduling

Administrators can define global data-handling tasks for activities and system components, while each course has its own recertification policy. Specialized providers are included for quizzes, forums, grades, activity completion, course completion, competencies and enrolments.

  • Recertification based on enrolment, course completion, a fixed annual date, certificate/reference providers or the last completed cycle.
  • Automatic, manual and bulk recertification workflows.
  • Simulation using the real providers inside a transaction that is always rolled back.
  • Permanent historical snapshots with optional structured JSON and copied files.
  • Notifications for warnings, availability, due dates, expiration, start and completion.
  • Backup support for course configuration and optional user history.
  • Privacy API support for cycles, history, files, logs and notification records.

Safe reset model

Generic cleanup is intentionally restricted to eligible activity tables and approved user conditions, while specialized subplugins can implement component-specific preservation and cleanup rules. This keeps the reset process controlled and traceable instead of deleting learner data without a recoverable history.

name: Video Mission
description: Turn a video into a mission-based activity with required or optional tasks tied to moments, intervals and questions.
description_html:
Activity module Video

Video Mission

Transform a video into a mission-based Moodle activity in which learners complete required or optional tasks tied to moments, intervals, questions and observations.

Plugin details

Component
mod_videomission
Moodle
4.4+
Source
Public GitHub repository
View source on GitHub

Main features

Six mission types

Create missions for a video moment, a video interval, a question, an observation, repeated occurrences or a simple task confirmation.

Mission rules and points

Mark missions as mandatory or optional, assign points and choose whether learners may complete them in any order or sequentially.

Real viewing progress

Tracks unique watched segments, total playback time, watched percentage and the learner's last position instead of assuming that reaching the end means the whole video was watched.

Reports and grading

Teachers can review mission status, responses, selected moments, earned points and watched percentage for each learner, with grades synchronized to the Moodle gradebook.

Completion rules

Activity completion can require all mandatory missions, a minimum watched percentage, or both.

Resume and seeking control

Playback can resume from the stored position and the activity can restrict seeking into portions of the video the learner has not yet watched.

Supported sources

Moodle upload Direct HTTP/HTTPS video URL YouTube Vimeo

Moodle integration

  • Backup and restore support.
  • Moodle Privacy API support.
  • External AJAX functions.
  • English and Brazilian Portuguese language packs.
  • Mustache templates and AMD JavaScript.

Why this activity exists

Video Mission transforma o vídeo em uma atividade orientada por objetivos. Em vez de considerar o play como participação suficiente, o professor define missões que exigem que o estudante encontre evidências, selecione momentos, delimite intervalos, responda perguntas, registre observações ou confirme tarefas.

Learning flow

1. Video as the context

The video is the source material and the timeline becomes part of the activity, not merely a media player.

2. Missions define the objective

Each mission tells the learner what must be found, explained, confirmed or observed.

3. Evidence is stored

Responses can include text, exact moments, intervals and repeated occurrence timestamps.

4. Progress is consolidated

The activity combines mission status, points and real watched-video progress.

What learners can do

Moment mission

The learner identifies one exact point in the video where the requested event or evidence occurs.

Interval mission

The learner defines a start and end point when the relevant evidence spans a period.

Question mission

A textual answer can be attached to the learning objective without separating it from the video activity.

Observation mission

The learner records an interpretation or observation based on the audiovisual evidence.

Occurrence mission

The activity can require several occurrences of the same event and preserve every selected timestamp.

Confirmation mission

A lightweight confirmation can be used when the mission represents a concrete task or verification.

Tracking and evidence

The tracking model stores unique watched segments, total playback time, last position and watched percentage. Rewatching does not artificially increase the unique percentage, while the total playback time still records repeated study. Seeking can also be restricted so the learner cannot jump far beyond portions already watched.

Teacher reports

Mission status

See completed, pending and locked missions for each learner.

Answers and evidence

Review text responses, moments, intervals and repeated occurrences.

Points

See points earned per mission and the consolidated score.

Viewing progress

Compare mission completion with the percentage of unique video content actually watched.

Gradebook

Mission points can be synchronized with the Moodle gradebook.

Completion

Completion can require mandatory missions, a minimum watched percentage, or both.

Typical uses

Case-based learningTechnical demonstrationsClinical observationMedia analysisProcedural trainingEvidence-finding activities

name: Video Diagnostic
description: Capture a pre-study diagnosis from video, release explanations and compare the learner's initial and later responses.
description_html:
Activity module Video

Video Diagnostic

Capture what learners understand before studying a video-based situation, release an explanation or study stage, and compare the initial diagnosis with a post-study response.

Plugin details

Component
mod_videodiagnostic
Moodle
4.4+
Source
Public GitHub repository
View source on GitHub

Main features

Before-and-after diagnosis

Collect an initial response before the explanation is shown and optionally ask the same diagnostic questions again after the study stage.

Multiple question formats

Use open responses, choices, video moments and video intervals so the diagnostic can measure both conceptual answers and evidence tied to the timeline.

Explanation stage

Provide an optional explanatory video, solution, teacher comments and complementary materials between the initial and final responses.

Automatic comparison

The activity compares initial and final answers so teachers can see how the learner's diagnosis changed after studying the explanation.

Optional diagnostic scoring

Expected answers, expected choices and expected video ranges can be used for automatic scoring; when no automatic criterion exists, the activity remains diagnostic-only.

Class and learner reports

Reports include selected timecodes, answer evolution, watched progress and CSV export.

Supported sources

Moodle upload Direct video URL YouTube Vimeo

Moodle integration

  • Server-side watched-segment tracking with unique watched percentage.
  • Large playback discontinuities are not counted as watched content.
  • Custom completion can require the initial submission and/or a watched percentage.
  • Backup and restore support, including user data when requested.
  • Moodle Privacy API support.
  • Diagnostic scores remain inside the activity and do not create a Moodle gradebook item.

Why this activity exists

Video Diagnostic foi pensado para diagnóstico de conhecimento prévio e mudança conceitual. O estudante responde antes da explicação, recebe a etapa de estudo e, quando habilitado, responde novamente às mesmas questões, permitindo comparar o raciocínio inicial com o que mudou depois do contato com o conteúdo.

Learning flow

1. Initial diagnostic

The learner watches the initial situation and answers before the explanatory material is released.

2. Baseline is preserved

The first response remains stored as the original diagnostic evidence.

3. Study stage is released

The activity can show an explanatory video, solution, teacher comments and complementary material.

4. Post-study comparison

A second response can be collected and compared directly with the initial one.

What learners can do

Open response

Capture the learner diagnosis or explanation in their own words.

Choice question

Use structured alternatives when the diagnostic requires a specific decision.

Video moment

Ask the learner to select the exact instant that supports the diagnosis.

Video interval

Capture evidence that spans a start and end point in the timeline.

Expected answers

Automatic criteria can be configured for text, options or expected video ranges when appropriate.

Diagnostic-only mode

When no automatic criterion exists, the activity remains diagnostic instead of manufacturing a grade.

Tracking and evidence

The activity periodically submits the real playback position and small contiguous watched intervals. The server merges accepted segments and calculates unique watched time and percentage, while large discontinuities are not accepted as watched content. This prevents a simple seek-to-end action from appearing as complete viewing.

Teacher reports

Initial response

Keep the answer submitted before study as the diagnostic baseline.

Final response

Show the post-study answer when the second response is enabled.

Answer evolution

Compare both responses side by side to make conceptual change visible.

Timecode evidence

Moment and interval selections remain attached to the learner response.

Class overview

Identify recurring misconceptions and patterns across learners.

CSV export

Export structured diagnostic data for further analysis.

Typical uses

Prior-knowledge assessmentMisconception analysisClinical reasoningCase diagnosisConceptual changeFormative assessment

description: Perform systematic video observation using teacher-defined events, timestamps, intervals and aggregate reports.
description_html:
Activity module Video

Video Observation

Run systematic video observation activities in which learners identify recurring events, record exact moments or intervals, and optionally attach notes to each observation.

Plugin details

Component
mod_videoobserve
Moodle
4.4+
Source
Public GitHub repository
View source on GitHub

Main features

Teacher-defined observation sheet

Teachers create reusable event types describing what learners should identify while watching the video.

Moment and interval observations

Students can mark a single instant or an interval and optionally add a textual note to explain what they observed.

Teacher reference observations

Teachers can register expected moments or intervals and compare learner marks against the reference using a configurable tolerance.

Aggregate analysis

Reports include event frequencies, time clusters, differences between learners, average markings and matches against the teacher reference.

Final observation sheet

The activity automatically consolidates the learner's markings into a final sheet and timeline.

Viewing progress

Watched segments and the last playback position are tracked alongside the observation data.

Supported sources

Moodle upload Direct video URL YouTube Vimeo

How it works

  1. Create the activity and select the video source.
  2. Create the event types in the observation sheet.
  3. Optionally register teacher reference observations.
  4. Learners watch the video and mark occurrences.
  5. Use the aggregate report to compare frequencies, time clusters, learners and reference matches.

Moodle integration

  • Uploaded videos and poster images are served through Moodle File API.
  • Custom completion can use watched percentage and number of observations.
  • Requires Moodle 4.4 or later.

Why this activity exists

Video Observation transforma observação audiovisual em dados estruturados. O professor define uma ficha com tipos de evento reutilizáveis e o estudante registra cada ocorrência no momento ou intervalo correspondente, podendo adicionar uma nota e depois comparar seu resultado com padrões da turma ou uma referência do professor.

Learning flow

1. Observation sheet

The teacher defines the events learners should identify.

2. Optional teacher reference

Expected moments or intervals can be recorded as a comparison baseline.

3. Learners mark occurrences

The same event can be registered repeatedly with point or interval evidence.

4. Aggregate analysis

The report compares frequencies, time clusters, learner differences and reference matches.

What learners can do

Reusable event types

Create named categories that define what learners should observe.

Point occurrence

Mark an event at one exact moment.

Interval occurrence

Represent events that span a period.

Optional notes

Add interpretation or context to each observation.

Teacher reference

Record expected observations separately from learner data.

Tolerance window

Define how close a learner mark must be to a reference mark to count as a match.

Tracking and evidence

Watched segments and the latest playback position are stored together with observation marks. This allows the teacher to separate a learner who watched little of the video from one who watched extensively but identified different events. Every observation also preserves its exact moment or interval.

Teacher reports

Final observation sheet

Review the learner complete set of observations.

Event frequency

Count how often each event type was identified.

Time clusters

Find moments where many learners placed observations.

Learner differences

Compare quantity and distribution of marks between students.

Reference matches

Review matches, missed expected marks and extra observations.

Completion

Require a minimum number of observations and/or watched percentage.

Typical uses

Classroom observationSports analysisClinical observationBehavior codingResearch analysisProcedure review
